s.n: Beer-battered onion rings with malt aioli
s.note: the local bar where Charlene works
s.how: Cut 2 large brown onions into 1cm rings and separate. Whisk 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and a pinch of salt with 250ml cold lager until just smooth. Dust the rings in flour, dip in the batter and fry in batches at 180C for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Salt straight away. Mix 150g mayonnaise with 1 tbsp malt vinegar and a crushed garlic clove for the dip.
Roast a 600g beef topside at 200C until 52C, rest and slice paper thin. Mix 3 tbsp barbecue sauce with 3 tbsp mayo. Pile the beef into 12 slider buns with the sauce and a slice of American cheese.

m.note: Lowell, the whole family at the table
m.how: Squeeze 400g Italian sausages from their skins and brown in a pan, breaking them up. Add 2 crushed garlic cloves, 700g passata and a pinch of chilli flakes and simmer 15 minutes. Boil 500g ziti or penne for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Toss with the sauce, spread in a baking dish and dot with 250g ricotta. Top with 200g grated mozzarella and 40g parmesan and bake at 200C for 25 minutes.

w.how: Whisk 4 eggs and 150g sugar until thick and fold in 150g self-raising flour. Bake in two tins at 175C for 20 minutes. Cook 400ml milk, 3 yolks, 80g sugar and 2 tbsp cornflour until thick and cool. Fill and pour over 150g chocolate melted with 100ml cream.

d.how: Chill four pint glasses in the freezer for 15 minutes. Pour a 375ml can of pale ale into each glass, tilting it so the head stays small. Hold a spoon upside down just above the beer and slowly pour 200ml Irish stout over the back of it so it floats in a dark layer on top. Serve straight away before the layers mix.
